paragraphs.text: Citation-first Socratic tutor for scanned books: DSH plugin + MCP server + FastAPI sidecar. Public c
orpora, federated search, policy-driven citation sources, SymPy/SciPy compute; every answer carries
an openable locator.
# socratic-tutor
**A citation-first Socratic tutor for scanned books.** Ask a question, get an answer that points at
a page you can actually open — on a personal library of 27 GB of PDFs, including Chinese classical t
exts read vertically, Latin, and Greek.
## Why this exists
Textbook chatbots answer from memory and cite nothing. For someone reading scanned editions — a punc
tuated `史記`, a Loeb volume, a 19th-century physics treatise — an answer you cannot check against the
page is worthless, and a fabricated citation is worse than no citation.
So the constraint here is inverted: **every claim must carry a locator (`book p.N`)**. With renderin
g enabled (the default) that locator resolves to a page image you can open; with `SOCRATIC_RENDER=of
f` it resolves to the indexed text of that page. Either way the citation is checkable, and the retri
eval layer is verified against whether that page actually contains the text it claims. When the syst
em cannot ground an answer, it is designed to say so rather than to improvise.
## What's in the box
| Component | What it is | Status |
| `plugin-socratic` | DSH plugin, **13 tools**: cited retrieval, lexical search, chapter lookup, pag
e images, math check, session review; embedded console with a policy card and per-citation tier/anch

or badges | npm `dsh-socratic@0.5.0` |
| `plugin-socratic-persona` | Teaching layer, **separate bund
le**: charter, per-step state summary, citation/leak/single-question rewriting. Install it for teach
ing; leave it out and the tools behave as an ordinary assistant | npm `dsh-socratic-persona@0.1.0` |
| `sidecar/` | FastAPI service: SQLite FTS5 + BGE-M3 + rerank + pypdfium2; public-corpus v2, federa
ted `scope=all/routed`, grep/lemma, SymPy/SciPy/pint/control, **citation policy** (`/v1/policy`) | *

*0.2.1**, Dockerfile + compose |
| `packages/classics-index` | Volume/chapter (`卷 / 篇 / 回`) indexer

for scanned Chinese books, built from OCR of running headers | PyPI `classics-index@0.1.3` |
| `pack
ages/socratic-mcp` | MCP server exposing search, lexical lookup, chapters, review and state | PyPI `
socratic-mcp@0.2.0` |

**0.3.x highlights** — public corpora v2 (Wikisource revisions / Perseus CTS URNs),
BGE-M3 hybrid re

trieval, Chinese→Greek/Latin query translation with an OOV gate,
grep/lemma channels, `scope=all` /

`scope=routed` federated search, and a
multi-backend compute endpoint with credentials and `disputed

ted` federated search, and a
multi-backend compute endpoint with credentials and `disputed` markers.

**0.4.x highlights** — citation policy as data: sources carry a trust tier
(`A`–`D`) and a role (`ci

te` / `template` / `verify`), channels describe how the
same source is reached (local file, RAG db,

public API, dataset, cloud), and the
subject rules pick the order. Ranking is deliberately *not* pol

icy-driven yet, so
the published retrieval numbers stay comparable; see
docs/CITATION-POLICY.md.

**0.5.x** — the teaching layer is its own bundle. `dsh-socratic` is now just the
tools and the conso

le; `dsh-socratic-persona` adds the charter, the state summary
and the stream rewrite. Presence, not

a flag, decides — so a development session
can use the tools without being turned into a student.
## Five page types it handles
The tutor is built around the layouts that break naive PDF pipelines: display math, horizontal Chine
se/English, vertical traditional Chinese, Latin, and polytonic Greek.
| display math | horizontal zh/en | vertical traditional |
| Latin with line numbers | Greek with breathings | |
These five images are **generated**, not scanned: see `eval/p3/make_sample_pages.py`. No copyrighted
page appears anywhere in this repository.

TRACT.md`. Any implementation that satisfies it can replace the sidecar; `scripts/contract_check.py`
makes that claim testable:

## Status and limitations
This is a single-machine, single-student research project, published so the pieces can be reused. Th
e honest scoreboard:
| Gate | Result |

| Citation resolves to a real page | **100%** (enforced server-side) |
| Page image renders | **100%

** |
| Answer-key leakage (266 probes) | **0** |
| Deterministic session review accuracy | **86.7%**

(23 held-out cases) |
| Monolingual retrieval recall | **0.82** — target 0.85, **not met** |
| Cros

s-lingual retrieval recall | **0.688** — target 0.70, **not met** |
| Human validation | **none yet*
* — every number above is machine-measured |
Known sharp edges: Greek OCR on degraded scans is unusable (the service falls back to page-image-onl
y results), the sidecar needs a GPU to be fast, and there is no async ingestion API yet — building a
library means running a script.
